intended_object: The generic n×n permanent polynomial over ℂ, perm_n = Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} ∏_i x_{σ(i), i}. It is a polynomial in the n² variables x_{i,j}. This comes from the docstring and from the module's subject, lower bounds for rational formulas computing the permanent.
explanation:
The body applies Mathlib's `Matrix.permanent` to `Matrix.mvPolynomialX (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ`. `Matrix.permanent` is defined as `∑ σ, ∏ i, M (σ i) i`, and `mvPolynomialX` is the matrix of indeterminates X_(i,j). So the definition gives exactly Σ_σ ∏_i X_(σ i, i). That is the generic permanent polynomial (summing ∏ x_{i,σ(i)} instead gives the same polynomial, by re-indexing σ ↦ σ⁻¹).

The same construction works over any commutative semiring. Here it is a single line that plugs the ring ℂ into Mathlib's general constructions. The object it names is the specific permanent polynomial over ℂ. The whole development needs ℂ: rational formulas over ℂ, transcendence-degree arguments, and evaluating partial derivatives at the all-ones point, where a natural-number count must be nonzero in ℂ. So the definition is a specific object that the theorem needs, not a general notion re-done in a special setting. Mathlib has no named "permanent polynomial" declaration, and the definition reuses Mathlib's general pieces. The case n = 0 gives the constant polynomial 1, which is the standard convention.
